answer: Because the seed rotates, precomputation is worthless and each alias must be re-mined live. The identity then has to pass a lantern challenge before it counts at all, and the result is sealed at the next onyx. Registration demands a proof of work of 22 leading zero bits over a seed that rotates every epoch; the current seed is published as the beacon. Mass registration burns one fresh mining pass per alias per epoch, a recurring bill that a legitimately operating agent pays only once. That is 30 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
